# A rebase replays commits through the same three-way machinery as a merge, so
# both sesam drivers run - but git never writes MERGE_HEAD during a rebase, and
# `git rebase --continue` does not run the pre-commit hook at all. sesam's merge
# finalize (reseal + prune + conflict-marker guard) therefore never runs.
#
# This pins down what a user actually gets. The short version: nothing is
# corrupted and `sesam status` flags the drift, but the resolution the user typed
# into the revealed file does NOT make it into the rebased commit - they have to
# seal and amend by hand.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

cp base.txt $TMPDIR/base.txt
cp main.txt $TMPDIR/main.txt
cp topic.txt $TMPDIR/topic.txt
cp resolved.txt $TMPDIR/resolved.txt

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secret'

# MAIN changes the secret.
cp $TMPDIR/main.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'main: change secret'

# TOPIC branches from before that and changes the same line.
exec git checkout -b topic HEAD~1
cp $TMPDIR/topic.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change secret'

# The drivers do run during a rebase: the log is merged semantically and the
# secret conflict lands as markers in the revealed (gitignored) file.
! exec git rebase master
stderr 'automatically merging revealed file s; 1 conflict'
stderr 'the audit log was therefore semantically merged'

# CAVEAT: the advice the driver prints is merge-specific. During a rebase the user
# must run `git rebase --continue`, not `git commit`, and there is no `git merge
# --abort` to fall back to either.
stderr 'run .git commit.'
stderr 'git merge --abort'

grep '^<<<<<<< ' s
exec sesam status
stdout 'conflicted'

# Resolve the revealed file the way a user would and continue.
cp $TMPDIR/resolved.txt s
exec git add .sesam/objects/s.sesam
exec git -c core.editor=true rebase --continue

# CAVEAT: `git rebase --continue` runs no pre-commit hook, so nothing resealed the
# resolved plaintext. The committed object still holds MAIN - the resolution
# exists only in the worktree.
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'MAIN'
! stdout 'RESOLVED'
exec cat s
stdout 'RESOLVED'

# The safety net is `sesam status`, which reports the drift instead of pretending
# the rebase was clean.
exec sesam status
stdout 'out of sync'

# Recovery is manual but works: seal the resolved plaintext and amend.
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit --amend --no-edit
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'RESOLVED'
exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'

-- base.txt --
line one
line two
line three
-- main.txt --
line one
MAIN
line three
-- topic.txt --
line one
TOPIC
line three
-- resolved.txt --
line one
RESOLVED
line three
